NFL: Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson out for rest of season after suffering knee injury during celebration
The Detroit Lions are set to be without star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson for the rest of the season after he suffered a torn ACL while celebrating a sack on Drake Maye during Sunday's win over the New England Patriots at Munich's Allianz Arena in Germany
Monday 16 November 2026 15:17, UK
Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson has been ruled out for the season after suffering a knee injury while celebrating a sack against the New England Patriots.
Hutchinson leaped in the air but went straight to the ground after landing. He immediately grabbed his right knee, staying down before eventually walking to the blue tent for evaluation.
He then walked gingerly to the locker room and didn't return to the game.
NFL Network Insider Ian Rapoport reported Monday that initial tests revealed Hutchinson sustained a torn ACL that will see him miss the rest of the season.

Hutchinson had sacked Maye on third down at the Detroit 15-yard line to end New England's opening drive, which saw Andy Borregales then kick a 33-yard field goal.
Maye also exited the game after the same play and is feared to have suffered a season-ending fractured ankle, with further tests expected upon his return to the United States.
The Lions went on to win the game 35-10 at Munich's Allianz Arena as the Patriots offense capitulated behind backup quarterback Tommy DeVito.
But it came at a major cost, with Detroit now set to resume their bid to reach a first Super Bowl minus their star pass rusher for the rest of the way.
Hutchinson has six sacks so far this year along with 50 pressures, following on from a 2025 season in which he led the team with a career-high 14.5 sacks.
Defensive end Derrick Moore impressed in Hutchinson's absence Sunday with two of the team's four sacks, with Alim McNeill also adding six pressures and increasing his sack tally to 6.5 on the year.
Hutchinson missed 12 games during the 2024 campaign after breaking his tibia and fibula.
Next up for the Lions, who are 7-2, is a meeting with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers before they host the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving.
